scenes.headline: Computational optics you can reproduce
scenes.narration: Fresnel turns physical optical targets into reproducible diffractive designs. It combines calculation, validation, fabrication exports, and experimental records in one open workflow.

scenes.headline: From one-off scripts to a real workflow
scenes.subheadline: Six optical design plugins share one production contract
scenes.narration: Diffractive optics is often demonstrated through isolated formulas or notebooks. Fresnel makes the workflow usable: zone plates, multi-focus elements, RGB designs, printable foils, macro cells, and computer-generated holograms all use the same application lifecycle.

scenes.headline: Start with the physical target
scenes.subheadline: 10 millimetre aperture · 1 metre focus · 532 nanometres · 1200 DPI
scenes.narration: The user specifies physical intent, not implementation code: aperture, focal distance, wavelength, printer resolution, mask type, and polarity. The schema-driven editor applies the same typed contract used by files, APIs, and tests.

scenes.headline: Validate before fabrication
scenes.narration: A preview is only a design aid. Before production, Fresnel performs deterministic optical and manufacturing checks. Warnings, metrics, assumptions, and quality reports remain separate from any generative explanation.

scenes.headline: The design is a portable production job
scenes.subheadline: .fresnel · versioned schema · stable plugin identity · content hash
scenes.narration: Every design can be saved as a versioned dot Fresnel job. It contains stable plugin identity, schema and algorithm versions, normalized parameters, production instructions, and provenance. The same file can be reopened, reviewed, rendered, and archived.

scenes.headline: One validated design, many real outputs
scenes.subheadline: PNG · SVG · PDF · DXF · Gerber · STL
scenes.narration: Once a design is production-ready, the same normalized parameters drive raster previews, vector exports, printable PDFs, laser-cutter outlines, Gerber fabrication files, and three-dimensional output where supported.

scenes.headline: The workflow extends beyond zone plates
scenes.subheadline: Target image → phase mask → reconstructed field
scenes.narration: The same architecture also supports iterative computer-generated holography. A bounded target image becomes a phase mask through the Gerchberg Saxton algorithm, with a reconstruction preview that makes the result inspectable.

scenes.headline: Documentation is executable evidence
scenes.subheadline: job → validation → renderer → artifact → manifest hash
scenes.narration: The documentation images are not hand-made illustrations. Checked-in jobs generate the artifacts, and a manifest records dimensions, resolution, parameter hashes, and normalized output hashes. Drift becomes a testable change instead of an undocumented screenshot.

scenes.headline: Fresnel
scenes.narration: Fresnel makes computational optics understandable and repeatable, from physical intent to a fabrication-ready result. The next hackathon step is a grounded natural-language experiment copilot built on top of these deterministic contracts.
